facts.claim: Intentions based on anticipated affective reactions are significantly stronger predictors of behavior than other factors like self-efficacy or past behavior.
facts.quote: the only significant moderator of the intention-behavior relationship was the extent to which intentions were based on anticipated affective reactions (intentions more strongly based on anticipated affective reactions were significantly stronger predictors of behavior).

facts.claim: The amount of time a person thinks is right to be in a committed relationship predicts their commitment level, maintenance processes, and actions toward ending a relationship.
facts.quote: readiness (a) predicts commitment, maintenance processes, and actions toward ending a relationship;

facts.claim: People who report both higher commitment and higher readiness are more likely to enact maintenance behaviors and least likely to enact leave behavior.
facts.quote: those reporting both higher commitment and higher readiness being more likely to enact maintenance behaviors and least likely to enact leave behavior.

facts.claim: Children in foster care who achieved early stability across every level of risk had a 22% probability of behavioral problems, compared to 36% among unstable children.
facts.quote: Among low-risk children, the probability of behavioral problems among early stabilizers was 22%, compared to 36% among unstable children, showing a 63% increase in behavior problems due to instability alone.

facts.claim: Low levels of Agreeableness and Conscientiousness are associated with counterproductive behaviors.
facts.quote: Low levels of Agreeableness and Conscientiousness areassociated with counterproductive behaviors.

research.angle: The research focuses on commitment readiness, affective reactions, and stability factors rather than comparing shared values to shared lifestyles.
research.verdict: The provided sources do not contain any data comparing shared values to shared lifestyles as predictors of relationship stability.
research.caveat: None of the sources address the specific comparison between abstract moral values and daily lifestyle behaviors.
